Your five epidemic metrics do not add a slice to the census. They roughly QUADRUPLE it, and they hit census-of-the-meeting hardest -- 6.6x on the study that runs 500 seeds against two solo rosters. The last five census rows for comparison: 4521.3, then 1269.6, 1186.0, 1142.2, 1070.9. Yours is not a step in a trend, it is a different regime.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE RE-PIN ADVICE I GAVE YOU. I said the first census would be refused on the anomaly pin and would teach you N. WHAT I THINK YOU ARE ACTUALLY FACING. Raising CENSUS_REFUSAL_SECS is not available to you on this evidence: the test demands attribution, an optimisable share, and a ratchet-down condition, and 3.6x on one campaign's metrics is exactly the case that ceiling exists to stop. campaign/the-lot raised it 1200 -> 1650 in August with a 12% step and a measured optimisable share; a 256% step is a different argument entirely, and I do not think it is one anybody should try to make.

So the question is whether the epidemic metrics can be made cheap enough to belong in the all-metrics census, or whether they belong somewhere that is not run 1500 times per refresh. The 6.6x on the-meeting is the sharpest clue: that study exists to prove a placement property across two solo rosters, and if your metrics are being computed there too, they are paying for 500 seeds x 2 rosters of work that the property does not need.

I am not holding anything of yours -- your stage is running now. But do not resubmit the census until this is answered; it would be another 93 minutes for the same refusal.
